implementerProof.how: The round's one claim — a period is a bucket of the database's clock rather than a window behind now, so a lone process makes a pass on every tick — was re-driven on the surface that found the defect it fixes: `go test -count=3 -run TestALoneRunnerMakesAPassOnEveryTick ./internal/dispatch/api/` → `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/api 35.446s`, where round 3 measured ran 7/6/6 and skipped 3/4/4. Round 3's other two claims were re-driven at this head too, on two real processes rather than in their own packages: the shutdown pair (below) and the document gate under concurrent cross-process writes. The whole two-process package is green here (`ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/dispatch`, every row), as is the browser suite (83 passed, 4 skipped, 6.3m), and CI is green on every lane at the code head 1be41dbb. The proof is verified; the failure below is a consequence of the bucket scheme that none of its rows reaches, because every row holds one lease to one period for the life of the test.
implementerProof.whatTheProofDidNotCover: No row anywhere drives one lease under two different periods, and one caller does exactly that at every convergence: docs.RunReferenceExcerptReconciliation passes the wait its last tick asked for, which alternates between referenceExcerptStep (2 s) and ReferenceExcerptReconcileInterval (5 min). The bucket number is floor(epoch / period), so those two periods number the clock on scales three orders of magnitude apart, and the gate compares them directly.

failures.criterion: Acceptance 1: "each background loop behaving as the plan's table says". The reference-excerpt reconciliation stops for good the first time it converges, and nothing says so.
failures.evidence: A period is now a bucket, `floor(extract(epoch from now()) / period)`, and the gate asks `duty_passes.bucket >= tick.bucket` (duty/exclusive.go, readPeriod). The bucket number therefore depends on the period: with a 2-second period it is about 8.96e8, with a 5-minute period about 5.98e6. docs.RunReferenceExcerptReconciliation is the one caller whose period changes between ticks — it passes the wait its last tick asked for, `referenceExcerptStep` (2 s) while a full batch says drift remains and `ReferenceExcerptReconcileInterval` (5 min) once none does (reference_excerpts.go, the `period = wait` line). So its first drift step records a bucket on the 2-second scale, and every later full-interval tick computes a bucket on the 5-minute scale, finds `896333757 >= 5975558`, and skips. It never recovers: the 5-minute scale does not reach 8.96e8 for about eight thousand years, the row is in the database rather than in a process, and a restart begins at the full interval and skips too. Measured, not argued: `Exclusive(ctx, leases, "reference-excerpts", 2*time.Second, …)` ran and recorded bucket 896333757; the next call at 5 minutes returned false and its pass never ran. The consequence is silent and user-visible — every mention a version write could not cut, and everything `rebuild-refs` inserts, keeps the document's name instead of its excerpt (refs.DriftedExcerpts, the loop's own doc comment), with no line saying the loop has stopped: it logs the ordinary `leased pass skipped`. Pinned by the red test TestExclusiveDoesNotLockOutALoopWhosePeriodGrows in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/duty/exclusive_test.go (commit cb82dc43), red at this head. The fix may be in either place — the gate made comparable across periods, or that loop stopped from varying the period it passes — but if the loop keeps its 2-second convergence step, which is its whole point when a rebuild leaves thousands of mentions owed, then the gate is where it has to be solved. Whichever is chosen, TestALoneRunnerMakesAPassOnEveryTick (api) and TestALeasedLoopRunsOnceAcrossAStaggeredStart (cmd/dispatch) must both stay green: they are the two properties the last two rounds bought.

notes: The bucket scheme has a property worth naming, which I am not recording as a failure: two passes can fall seconds apart across a bucket boundary, so a period bounds the work at one pass per aligned bucket rather than one pass per any window of that length. For the GitHub rate limit, which is what the leases were chosen for, that bound is what matters; for a reader it is invisible.
